title: Rupa & Company Ltd - 533552 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Rupa Q1 FY27 revenue rose 10.1% YoY to Rs 202.4 crore, EBITDA margin 7.8% (+120 bps) and PAT up 50.2% to Rs 8.3 crore.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 10.1% YoY to Rs 202.4 crore, driven by volume, with the value segment the main contributor. EBITDA rose 29.1% to Rs 15.7 crore at a 7.8% margin, and PAT rose 50.2% to Rs 8.3 crore. Management said a price hike taken in April was largely passed on to trade through extra schemes, so realisations did not capture it. Management guided to 10-12% revenue growth and a 9-10% EBITDA margin for the coming quarter, with a further price hike planned for August.

financial_highlights.metric: Modern trade including e-commerce share of revenue

financial_highlights.value: About Rs 21 crore, about 10.5% of revenue

segments.name: Athleisure
segments.commentary: Q1 declined 5-7% YoY after a strong Q4; management targets at least double-digit growth from Q2 and more than double-digit for the full year.

segments.name: Women's wear (Softline, Macroman)
segments.commentary: Women's share was about 8% in Q1 and has run at 8-10% on an annual basis. Softline is undergoing a brand and font change, with new fabrics and a new team being built.

segments.name: Thermal (winterwear)
segments.commentary: Management described the order book as sound and expects FY27 thermal sales to be better than last year, but this depends on how the winter unfolds.

segments.name: E-commerce and modern trade
segments.commentary: Management targets 20-25% e-commerce growth, with senior heads appointed and warehousing, inventory and IT infrastructure being built.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth of 10-12% expected in the coming quarter (Q2 FY27).
EBITDA margin expected to stay in the 9-10% range in the coming quarter.
A further price hike of 4-5% is planned to be implemented from August, dependent on competitor behaviour.
Advertising and marketing spend to be rationalised from about 10.5% of revenue to 6-7%, which management says will support the EBITDA margin target.
Athleisure expected to grow at least double digits from Q2 and more than double digits for the full year; e-commerce targeted at 20-25% growth.
capex_capacity: No capacity, utilisation or capex figures were disclosed on the call.
Management said a DMS (distributor management system) is being rolled out state by state, with a hands-on presence expected in a year or two; ARS is described as in place but dependent on DMS.
demand_pricing: Q1 price hike of 4-5% was largely passed to trade through extra schemes because of intense competition, so realisations did not reflect it; growth was volume-led.
Gross margin slipped 30 bps YoY to 37.4%.
Yarn prices are rising, which management sees as a favourable pricing environment, but competitors are offering extra discounts and extended sale periods to gain share.
Old inventory across the industry is described as now largely exhausted, with fresh stock at higher prices, which management expects will allow the new rate to stick from August.
Management said competition is mainly from organised players and that Rupa is taking share, but via higher discounts.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall short of the 9-10% guidance given last quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said advertising and marketing spend was about 10.5% of revenue in Q1 and would be rationalised to 6-7%, which should help achieve the desired EBITDA level.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the April price hike not show up in realisations, and when will it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said intense competition led to extra schemes that passed the hike on to trade. A new rate is expected from August, and it is yet to be implemented.

qa_highlights.question: What is the thermal order book outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Sound and healthy order book; management expects thermal to contribute better than last year, but this depends on how the winter season unfolds.

qa_highlights.question: Will further price hikes be taken to offset yarn cost inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, a further hike is planned, but it depends on how competitors behave.

qa_highlights.question: What were the athleisure and women's trends, and what is planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Athleisure fell 5-7% YoY in Q1 and is targeted at double-digit growth from Q2. Women's share is about 8%, and Softline is being rebranded and gets a new team and fabrics.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ROCE/ROE decline structural, and is there room to cut costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the returns are not desirable and blamed the tough competitive environment. It cited the shift from wholesale to secondary-led sales, LFS, e-commerce and other channels. Cost efficiency is an ongoing process with no fixed target.

risks_watch: Competitive intensity from organised players continues to drive extra schemes, so price hikes may not stick (the April hike was largely passed on).
Whether the planned August price hike is implemented and reflected in realisations.
Thermal sales depend on the timing and severity of the winter season.
Women's wear and athleisure both declined or underperformed in Q1; the recovery is not yet proven.
Management guided 9-10% EBITDA margin last quarter but reported 7.8%; the cut in ad spend to 6-7% of revenue needs to show up next quarter.
summary.management_tone: Optimistic on volumes, channels and pricing outlook, but cautious and hedged on price realisation, thermal and women's wear. Responses on competition and returns were often open-ended and deferred to coming quarters.
key_quotes: So, from August onward, we are quite hopeful the new rate will be implemented.
When there is a scope of 2%, there is a scope of another 2%, we have to do it.

growth.why: Management guides 10-12% revenue growth for Q2 FY27 with a 9-10% EBITDA margin, backed by a planned 4-5% August price hike, competitive discounting and volume gains, but no capacity, order or contract figures were given, so backing is vague.
